project.name: ChatFlow Backend
project.description: Chat backend built with Node.js, strict TypeScript, Koa, PostgreSQL (Drizzle ORM + pg), and Firebase Firestore (firebase-admin).
project.scope: ====-only API service (no frontend required by the task).

techStack.relationalDb: PostgreSQL (Neon / pg + Drizzle ORM) for users, chats, and chat_members
techStack.documentDb: Firebase Firestore for messages, read receipts, and last seen tracking
techStack.authentication: JWT Bearer tokens (HS256) + bcrypt password hashing

requestPipeline: 1. Koa CORS & Root Error Boundary (src/app.ts) catches any parsing or unhandled errors and formats them cleanly.
2. @koa/router matches the route and invokes the endpoint's composed hook chain.
3. useKoa() builds normalized Request Props and maps returned objects or thrown AppError subclasses to standard JSON responses.
4. useServices() injects PostgreSQL (db), Firestore (firestore), Logger (logger), and module services.
5. useLogging() logs method, path, HTTP status, and latency in milliseconds.
6. useAuth() (on protected endpoints) verifies Authorization: Bearer <token>, loads the active user from PostgreSQL, and injects args.currentUser.
7. usePathParams() / useQueryString() / useJsonBody() validate inputs via Zod schemas and throw 400 BadRequestError with field details on invalid input.
8. Service & Repository layers execute business rules and interact with PostgreSQL and/or Firestore.

whyTwoDatabases.postgresql: Stores users, chats (1:1 and group), and chat_members. Guarantees referential integrity (FKs), ACID transactions, fast membership joins, and atomic 1:1 chat deduplication via UNIQUE(chats.direct_key).
whyTwoDatabases.firestore: Stores high-frequency message streams (chats/{chatId}/messages/{messageId}), read receipts (.../readReceipts/{userId}), and last seen pointers (chats/{chatId}/lastSeen/{userId}) with timestamp ordering and horizontal scalability.

interactionBetweenDatabases: Step A (Auth & Identity): User registers/logs in -> stored/verified in PostgreSQL users table -> receives JWT.
Step B (Chat Creation): POST /chat/create verifies both users are active in PostgreSQL, computes sorted direct_key, and atomically creates or fetches the chat + chat_members rows in PostgreSQL.

Step C (Send Message): POST /chat/:chatId/message/send verifies JWT + checks chat_members in PostgreSQL -> writes message document with timestamp to Firestore -> updates chats.updated_at in PostgreSQL.
Step D (Fetch Messages): GET /chat/:chatId/messages verifies chat_members in PostgreSQL -> queries Firestore messages ordered by createdAt + fetches lastSeen map.

Step E (Read Receipt & Last Seen): POST .../read and POST .../lastseen verify membership in PostgreSQL and message existence in Firestore -> atomically update Firestore readBy/readReceipts and lastSeen.

success.pagination: (optional, returned on paginated endpoints like GET /users)

error.details: (optional array/object, e.g. Zod field validation errors)

quickStartTestingOrder: 1. GET /health/status -> verify PostgreSQL and Firestore are connected.
2. POST /user/register (Alice) -> save data.user.id as USER_A_ID and data.token as TOKEN_A.
3. POST /user/register (Bob) -> save data.user.id as USER_B_ID and data.token as TOKEN_B.
4. POST /chat/create with { userAId, userBId } and TOKEN_A -> save data.chatId as CHAT_ID.
5. POST /chat/{CHAT_ID}/message/send with { senderId: USER_A_ID, text } and TOKEN_A -> save data.message.id as MESSAGE_ID.
6. GET /chat/{CHAT_ID}/messages?limit=50 with TOKEN_B -> verify message list ordered by timestamp.
7. POST /chat/{CHAT_ID}/message/{MESSAGE_ID}/read with { userId: USER_B_ID } and TOKEN_B -> verify read receipt updated.
8. POST /chat/{CHAT_ID}/lastseen with { userId: USER_B_ID, messageId: MESSAGE_ID } and TOKEN_B -> verify last seen updated.
9. GET /user/{USER_A_ID}/chats with TOKEN_A -> verify chat list with memberIds from PostgreSQL.
10. (Bonus) Test PATCH/DELETE message and POST /chat/group/create + group member management.

endpoints.name: Health & Connectivity Check
endpoints.howItWorks: Pings both PostgreSQL (SELECT 1) and Firebase Firestore (listCollections) and reports 200 (ok) or 503 (degraded).

endpoints.name: Register User
endpoints.howItWorks: Validates input via Zod, checks email/username uniqueness in PostgreSQL, hashes password with bcrypt, inserts user, and returns a signed HS256 JWT.

endpoints.name: Login User
endpoints.howItWorks: Finds user by normalized email in PostgreSQL, compares password hash with bcrypt, verifies active status, updates last_active_at, and returns a JWT.

endpoints.name: Get Current User Profile
endpoints.howItWorks: useAuth() validates the Bearer JWT and returns the authenticated user profile.

endpoints.name: Update Current User Profile
endpoints.howItWorks: Updates name, username (with uniqueness check), or avatarUrl for the authenticated user in PostgreSQL.
endpoints.curl: curl -X PATCH http://localhost:8000/user/me -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN_A>" -d '{"name":"Alice Updated","username":"alice_updated"}'

endpoints.name: Get User By ID
endpoints.howItWorks: Validates UUID path parameter and fetches sanitized public user data from PostgreSQL.

endpoints.name: List / Search Users
endpoints.howItWorks: Queries PostgreSQL users table with optional search/status filters and returns paginated users.

endpoints.name: 1. Create or Get 1:1 Chat
endpoints.howItWorks: Verifies authenticated user is one of userAId/userBId, verifies both users exist and are active in PostgreSQL, builds canonical direct_key (sorted UUIDs), and atomically creates or returns the existing 1:1 chat with members.

endpoints.name: 2. Send Message
endpoints.howItWorks: Verifies senderId matches authenticated user and checks chat membership in PostgreSQL. Stores message document with server Timestamp in Firestore (chats/{chatId}/messages/{messageId}) and updates chats.updated_at in PostgreSQL.

endpoints.name: 3. Get Messages

queryParams.before: optional messageId cursor for loading older messages
queryParams.order: asc (default, oldest-to-newest of latest slice) | desc

endpoints.howItWorks: Verifies chat membership in PostgreSQL, queries Firestore messages ordered by createdAt, and fetches the chat's lastSeen map.

endpoints.name: 4. Mark Message Read
endpoints.howItWorks: Verifies userId matches authenticated user, checks PostgreSQL membership & Firestore message existence, then atomically updates readBy.<userId> on the message and upserts chats/{chatId}/messages/{messageId}/readReceipts/{userId}.

endpoints.name: 5. Update Last Seen Message
endpoints.howItWorks: Verifies userId matches authenticated user, checks PostgreSQL membership and Firestore message existence, then upserts chats/{chatId}/lastSeen/{userId}.

endpoints.name: 6. List User Chats
endpoints.howItWorks: Verifies userId matches authenticated user and fetches all chats and member IDs for that user from PostgreSQL in a single join+subquery ordered by updated_at DESC.

endpoints.name: Create Group Chat
endpoints.howItWorks: Validates all members are active in PostgreSQL, automatically includes the authenticated creator as admin, and creates the group chat + members transactionally.

endpoints.name: Get Chat Details
endpoints.howItWorks: Verifies chat membership in PostgreSQL and returns chat metadata and member list.

endpoints.name: Rename Group Chat
endpoints.howItWorks: Verifies chat is a group chat and caller has admin role, then updates chat name in PostgreSQL.

endpoints.name: Add Group Members
endpoints.howItWorks: Verifies group admin role and active status of all target users, then adds members idempotently.

endpoints.name: Remove Group Member / Leave Group
endpoints.howItWorks: Allows a group admin to remove any member, or any member to remove themselves (leave group).

endpoints.name: Edit Message
endpoints.howItWorks: Verifies membership and original sender ownership; rejects if message is already deleted; updates text, isEdited=true, editedAt in Firestore.

endpoints.name: Soft-Delete Message
endpoints.howItWorks: Verifies membership and original sender ownership, then soft-deletes the message in Firestore (isDeleted=true, deletedAt, clears text).
